name: The Dvaita sequence of means (sādhana-krama)

stages.name: adhikāra, vairāgya
stages.description: Eligibility by nature, class and qualities; for the highest, dispassion that sees everything from Brahmā to a blade of grass as worthless and impermanent, and sole refuge in Viṣṇu.

stages.name: sadācāra, niṣkāma-karma
stages.description: Prescribed duties done without desire and offered to Hari as the real doer; vows such as Ekādaśī.

stages.name: guru-upasatti, dīkṣā
stages.description: Gaining the supreme knowledge from the grace of a teacher; initiation into Hari's worship.

stages.name: śravaṇa
stages.description: Study of the true scriptures with Madhva's commentaries.

stages.name: manana
stages.description: Reasoned reflection removing doubts.

stages.name: dhyāna / nididhyāsana, upāsanā
stages.description: Meditation on Hari with qualities fit for the meditator, within the heart as one's original (bimba).

stages.name: bhakti
stages.gloss: devotion grounded in knowledge of God's greatness
stages.description: Firm love exceeding all other love; accompanies and crowns every stage.

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: Direct realization of the Lord, as fitness allows; the gods are liberated when Hari becomes directly perceived.

stages.name: paramātma-prasāda
stages.description: Won by fullness of knowledge; without it there is no liberation.

stages.name: mokṣa
stages.description: Release into one's own bliss in the Lord's presence (see pth:dvaita-moksa-krama).

notes: A composite ordering of means that Madhva and the tradition name in several places (BSB 1.1.1; MBTN 1.85–99; Nyāyāmṛta 3; Yogadīpikā 1). The texts do not give this exact ten-step list; the sequence and the bands are the interpretation layer. Bhakti and grace are not a single 'stage' for the tradition: bhakti accompanies every step, and grace alone liberates.

name: From direct knowledge to liberation (Dvaita)

stages.name: aparokṣa-jñāna
stages.description: The knower sees the Lord (as fitness allows); acquired karma no longer binds.

stages.name: prārabdha-bhoga
stages.description: The knower remains embodied until the karma in effect is spent.

stages.name: utkrānti
stages.description: At death the tip of the heart lights up and the knower leaves by the crown channel, helped by Hari in the heart; some are liberated without departing.

stages.name: arcirādi-mārga
stages.description: The knower goes by the path of light to Brahmā's world.

stages.name: brahmaṇā saha mokṣa
stages.description: At the great dissolution those in Brahmā's world reach the Supreme together with Brahmā.

stages.name: mukti-bhoga
stages.description: Sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya or sāyujya; bliss graded a hundredfold by class; desires in accord with the Lord's; bhakti continuing as eternal bliss.

notes: Assembled from Madhva's Brahmasūtrabhāṣya 3–4; the order of stages follows the sūtras. Bands are interpretive; B8 for prārabdha-bhoga is a correspondence of position only — Dvaita does not treat the embodied knower as already liberated in the sense of final mokṣa.

name: The Yogadīpikā's graded disciplines

stages.name: śauca, āsana, prāṇāyāma, aparigraha, ahiṃsā, satya, asteya, brahmacarya, tapas, tuṣṭi
stages.gloss: purity, posture, breath, restraints and observances
stages.description: Listed first, of least weight.

stages.name: yajña and other duties, svādhyāya, hari-arcana
stages.description: Of greater weight.

stages.name: śravaṇa, manana
stages.description: Never to be reduced.

stages.name: vyākhyāna of the Upaniṣads, bhakti
stages.description: Of the greatest weight.

notes: The text ranks these disciplines in ascending importance ('each later one with special weight'); it does not present them as successive stages. Reading them as a path map is interpretive.
